newsitem.title: USA: Chip industry ratio rises in November.
newsitem.headline: Chip industry ratio rises in November.

text.p: The semiconductor industry's key indicator rose last month to the highest level in more than a year, reflecting a 6.3 percent increase in orders for computer chips.

The Semiconductor Industry Association Monday said its book-to-bill ratio, which measures the value of orders against shipments, rose to 1.15 in November from a revised 1.11 in October. The ratio means manufactures received $115 in new orders last month for every $100 in shipments.

Industry analysts had expected the ratio to be flat to slightly higher than October's level so the stronger than-expected performance last month could give chip stocks' like Intel Corp., Micron Technology Inc. and Texas Instruments Inc., a boost on Tuesday.

The ratio, a leading indicator of future demand tallied by the industry trade group, has been improving recently, reflecting an increase in orders by personal computer makers and more stable prices for memory chip prices.

In March, the index hit its lowest point in years when it dropped to 0.79, reflecting a glut of computer chips in the market. Since then it has been rising steadily as inventory levels have stabilized.
In a statement, the trade group said the November ratio was the highest since October of 1995, when it jumped to 1.16.
Fueling the rise was a 6.3 percent jump in new orders last month to $3.96 billion, coupled with a 2.9 percent rise in shipments to $3.44 billion.
The October ratio was revised from 1.10.
Association officials said the increase in November marked the fourth consecutive month of real increases in orders and the third straight month of higher shipments.

"Given all that has happened in 1996, it's best to use caution in evaluating these numbers," said Doug Andrey, director of information systems for the association. "But they are undeniably the best marks we've seen for the Americas market all year. The third-quarter doldrums are behind us."

The book-to-bill ratio, which covers the Americas market, is due to be replaced next year by a global index. The Semiconductor Industry Association said the worldwide ratio for October, the latest period available, was 1.09.
While up from October, last month's orders were 19.4 percent below the year-ago period while shipments were 20.7 percent below November of 1995.
